The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Quay County in east central New Mexico...
Southeastern Harding County in northeastern New Mexico...

* Until 100 AM MDT.

* At 1009 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.75 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Quay and Southeastern Harding
Counties.

Flash flooding is expected along McCarty Road and Nara Visa Road near
the Quay and Harding County border.

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* Until 1145 PM MDT.

* At 954 PM MDT, Thunderstorms with torrential rainfall continue to
roll across parts of central Hudspeth County, north of Sierra
Blanca. 0.50 to 1.50 inches of rain has fallen across rural areas
between Cornudas and Sunset Ranches, west of FM-1111.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of arroyos and draws, roads, and low water
crossings, as other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornudas and areas north of Sunset Ranches.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
South Well Draw, Eightmile Draw, University Draw, and others.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...The Flood Watch remains in effect for southwestern New
Mexico and far west Texas through Wednesday evening.

* WHERE...Southwestern New Mexico and far west Texas.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season plume of deep tropical moisture is transported
northward ahead of an upper-level disturbance, bringing several
rounds of thunderstorms with high rainfall rates to the region
through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may result in
isolated to scattered instances of flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
